mind_map.root_node: Grandmother’s Quilt (Perimeter Boundary, Area Surface & Grid Optimization)

key_nodes: Perimeter Definition: Continuous outer boundary distance surrounding a 2D closed figure
Linear Measurement Units: Measured in centimetres (cm), metres (m), kilometres (km)
Additive Boundary Principle: Summing all outer side lengths of any polygon
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Including internal grid lines when calculating the perimeter of a compound shape.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Perimeter = Sum of all outer boundary side lengths.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Stitching lace borders around quilts, fencing garden plots, and picture framing.

key_nodes: Perimeter of Rectangle: P = 2 x (Length + Breadth) = 2(L + B)
Perimeter of Square: P = 4 x Side length = 4S
Perimeter of Regular Polygon: P = Number of sides (N) x Side length (S)
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Adding length and breadth once for rectangle perimeter instead of multiplying sum by 2.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Calculating jogging track perimeter and baseboard molding lengths.

key_nodes: Area Definition: Total 2D surface region enclosed inside a closed shape boundary
Square Measurement Units: Measured in square centimetres (sq cm), square metres (sq m)
Surface Coverage: Tiling surface with unit squares without gaps or overlaps
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Expressing area in linear units (cm) instead of square units (sq cm).
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Area Units: 1 sq cm = Area of square with 1 cm side length.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Calculating room floor tiling, quilt patch fabrics, and farm field land areas.

key_nodes: Area of Rectangle: Area = Length x Breadth (A = L x B)
Area of Square: Area = Side x Side (A = S²)
Derived Side Formula: Side of Square = Sqrt(Area); Breadth of Rectangle = Area / Length
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Multiplying side by 4 to find square area instead of squaring the side.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Area Formulas: A_rectangle = L x B; A_square = S².
sub_branches.real_world_application: Buying carpet rolls, painting wall surfaces, and land parcel sales.

sub_branches.sub_title: Grid Square Tiling & Partial Square Rules
key_nodes: Grid Square Counting Rules: Full square = 1 unit; Half square = 0.5 unit; Greater-than-half square = 1 unit; Less-than-half square = 0 units
Tracing Irregular Objects: Estimating area of hand palms and leaves on centimetre grid paper
Tiling Efficiency: Counting total unit tiles needed to cover a quilt bed
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Counting less-than-half squares as full squares during grid area estimation.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Grid Area Estimation = Full Squares + (0.5 x Half Squares) + Greater-Than-Half Squares.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Estimating leaf surface areas in biology and footprint tracking.

key_nodes: Area-Perimeter Independence: Shapes with identical areas can have completely different perimeters (e.g., 1x12 rectangle P=26m vs 3x4 rectangle P=14m, both Area=12 sq m)
Square Optimization Principle: Among all rectangles with a fixed perimeter, a SQUARE encloses maximum surface area
Perimeter Minimization: Among all rectangles with a fixed area, a SQUARE has the minimum perimeter
sub_branches.misconception_alert: Assuming two shapes with equal perimeters must have equal areas.
sub_branches.formula_or_rule: Optimization Principle: Square shape maximizes area for any given fixed perimeter length.
sub_branches.real_world_application: Maximizing garden bed area with fixed fencing wire and optimizing quilt patchwork.
